rounds.scope: protocol draft, generator, runner, analyzer, roster (independent-draw design)

findings.area: design: H and L are collateral relatives, so the null overstates the post-midpoint change
findings.detail: H is an independent mass-weighted draw from the 500k population and is paired with L only by draw index (tools/lib/discovery-continuation.ts:243). Reconstructing lineages from the recorded mutation-parent edges (own script, ancestry.ts) shows that in only 7 of 64 pairs (cluster-33: 6, cluster-4: 1) is H on L's lineage. In 57 pairs H is a collateral relative: 32 meet only at the founder lineage (cluster-16 16/16, cluster-4 13/16, cluster-139 3/16) and 25 at a later ancestor (median MRCA birth about 136k steps). The H->L difference is therefore the symmetric difference of two independent branches (H's private changes undone plus L's private changes), mean 28.9 slots (cluster-16 43.4, cluster-139 30.8, cluster-4 24.6, cluster-33 16.8), whereas L's own change since its 500k ancestor averages 12.4 slots (cluster-16 16.2, cluster-139 15.1, cluster-33 10.6, cluster-4 7.8). The type-matched null (lib:258-262) copies the whole symmetric difference onto H, so N carries about 2.3x (1.6x to 3.1x by founder) the change that L actually accumulated since the midpoint, keeps all of H's private changes and cannot model their reversal. The protocol's question and null description ('random mutants of the midpoint genome carrying the same amount and kind of genetic change', 'change since the midpoint') are not true of the roster. L-N > 0 can arise with no adaptation (N is a degraded H), and L vs H measures a population-level difference between typical 1M and typical 500k members, which can also reflect standing diversity and non-transitivity between collaterals. The estimand is defensible as a population comparison but is not what the text says, and the null is not the divergence control's ancestor-descendant null.
findings.fix: Preferred: pair each L draw with its own 500k ancestor A(L): the lineage on L's path with the largest birth step <= 500k. It is always alive at the 500k state (it has a child born later), and I verified A(L) exists as a single genome for all 64 L draws. H=A(L) makes every pair ancestor-descendant, the null the exact analogue of the divergence control, and the H sampling seeds unnecessary; the roster, runner and 1,536-competition budget are otherwise unchanged. It needs a new generator step, tests and a re-review. Minimum if the independent-draw design is kept: rewrite the question, the null and the M4 claims to state the population-level estimand and that the null overstates the change; compute per-pair relation (ancestral vs collateral, MRCA birth, A->L distance) in the generator from existing edges and put it in the roster; pre-register descriptive stratification by relation; optionally add 512 descriptive L-vs-A(L) competitions (about 1.8 h) as a direct within-lineage measure.

findings.area: protocol: M4 table over-reads 'not met' and omits outcomes
findings.detail: Row 'Not met, L ~ H' concludes 'adaptation stalls ... supports the registered pivot', but (a) L ~ H has no operational definition anywhere in the protocol or analyzer; (b) the analyzer's own reading says not-met is 'not evidence that adaptation stopped' (lib:436); (c) the design has little power for moderate effects. From the divergence control's per-draw scores the within-seed SD of one evolved draw is 0.02/0.28/0.19/0.22 and of one matched mutant 0.54/0.66/0.15/0.34 (cluster-33/4/16/139), so a unit contrast (2 L draws, 4 nulls) has SD about 0.15-0.4. With the 0.10 per-seed bar and 7/8 rule, P(met) at a true contrast of 0.3 is about 0.29 (SD 0.35) to 0.47 (SD 0.25) to 0.84 (SD 0.15); at 0.5 it is 0.73-1.0; at 0.2 it is 0.12-0.36. A 'not met' is therefore the expected outcome for real but moderate continued adaptation, and cannot support the physics-change pivot. Also missing: a row for 'met, purifying only' (a reachable outcome with L ~ 0 when N is degraded); a rule for which founders decide M4 (line 63 says cluster-33 matters most, line 69 says mixed means no pivot); and what a positive cluster-16 reading means (the stated no-adaptation reference).
findings.fix: Before freezing: (1) replace row 2 with 'Not met: inconclusive for M4, no stall claim' unless an equivalence rule is pre-registered (for example founder-level L point estimate and unit-bootstrap upper bound both below a stated value); (2) add rows for purifying-only and for a cluster-16 reading of continued/partly ('assay or design is not detecting adaptation; other readings uninterpretable'); (3) state which founder tests the M4 table is applied to and how mixed founder results combine; (4) add one sentence that the study can only detect large continued gains (unit contrast of roughly 0.4-0.5 or more) in typical seeds.

findings.area: confirmatory criterion does not itself encode progress
findings.detail: 'Met' is 7/8 units with L-N lower bound > 0.10 (lib:494, 512). Progress (L vs H > 0.10) enters only through the founder-level mean L lower bound in the reading (lib:438), not per seed. Because N is a degraded H, L-N can exceed 0.10 in 7/8 seeds with L about 0 ('purifying only', lib:438-440), and a founder can be 'continued' on a mean L that one or two large seeds carry (in the divergence control cluster-4 seed 6410008 had E=-0.74 against its founder). The protocol's headline question (do 1M descendants beat 500k descendants by more than random mutants) reads as if 'met' implied progress.
findings.fix: Report, and preferably include in the 'continued' reading, the number of seeds with L vs H lower bound > 0.10 (same 7/8 rule), or state explicitly that 'met' alone means only 'better than a degraded midpoint'.

findings.area: design: no control for standing diversity or non-transitivity
findings.detail: The 500k and 1M populations are mutant swarms (distinct genomes at 500k: cluster-33 45-58, cluster-4 154-250, cluster-16 386-410, cluster-139 64-471; no genome above 6% in cluster-16 and none above 1.3% in 5 of 8 cluster-139 seeds). A randomly drawn H is one member of a cloud, and L vs H mixes adaptation with member-to-member variation. Nothing measures the exchangeable baseline (two same-time draws), so the spread of L vs H cannot be compared with pure sampling noise.
findings.fix: Optional but cheap: 256 competitions of H0 vs H1 (32 units x 8, about 0.9 h) and, if desired, L0 vs L1, give an empirical noise floor and a same-time null; or rely on the ancestor pairing in F1.

findings.area: cluster-139 and cluster-33 sweep status at 500k is stated incorrectly or loosely
findings.detail: From roster.json (sweep.ts): cluster-33 H draws carry the raised b2[PHOTO] (>62) in 14/16 draws (seed 6410002 neither H nor L carries it); L carries a further increase in seed 6410006 (99->119, 82->99). cluster-139: H carries the mu sweep (>=45) in 14/16 draws; only seed 6410007 (both draws) has H=33 and L=47, a sweep that falls after 500k; in seeds 6410002 (both draws) and 6410008 (draw 1) L has mu=33 while H has 54-55, i.e. L has lost the swept allele. So the 'sweep tail' worry is confined to one cluster-139 seed, and the larger interpretive problem is reversal or alternative routes, which an L-N contrast cannot call adaptation. Separately, the type-matched null copies each mu change with a random sign, so about half of the nulls of seed 6410007 reproduce the sweep and half of seed 6410002's reproduce L's mu=33 (the mirror-sign bias already documented for the divergence control).
findings.fix: State these counts in the protocol as descriptive pre-run facts, say cluster-139 is not read for M4 'after the first sweep', and compute the sweep-carriage table in the analyzer (F6).

findings.area: sampling: restated sampler and truncated-chain loader
findings.detail: sampleState equals the frozen computation for everything that determines the draws (founder root, rootMasses with ancestryResolver, sampleRoot with Random(seed).int53). I reproduced it with independent code: all 32 histories' midpoint draws, rootMass, distinct-genome counts, state hashes, receipt SHA-256s and seeds match roster.json, and the same code reproduces all 64 frozen 100k and 1M samples including abundance-table order. Omitted from sampleDiscoveryEvolution: validateEdges' id-pattern/leading-zero and lineageKey round-trip checks, and the per-occupied-cell canonical re-encoding and hex round-trip checks. validateCheckpointBiology (run by the loader at 500k) covers edge shape/causality/cycles/conflicts, founder-lineage genome identity and the founding-root check; rootMasses covers padding and conflicting lineage words. Uncovered at 500k only: the canonical encode/decode round trip of every occupied cell, which the hash-pinned state makes a simulator invariant. A malformed edge id would produce unknown ancestry and refuse the draw, not change it silently. Truncated chain: tampered 500k and 300k checkpoints, an edited edge delta, a missing triple, a swapped receipt and a non-checkpoint step are all refused (negative.ts); the 500k receipt is also anchored by the 1M-chain load done first. One gap: verifyCheckpointInventory runs on the scratch hard-link directory, so a stray file in the real history directory is not detected (tested: no error).
findings.fix: Optional hardening: call the frozen sampleDiscoveryEvolution on { ...state, step: 1_000_000 } (all edges are <= 500k so validateEdges passes) and use its draws, which runs every frozen check on the 500k state; optionally run verifyCheckpointInventory on the real history directory.

review.designAssessment: The code, roster and analysis are sound and independently reproduced, and nothing in the released-candidate path can confuse this study with the divergence control. The weaknesses are in what the experiment measures. (1) H and L are independent draws from two mutant swarms, collateral relatives in 57 of 64 pairs and meeting only at the founder lineage in 32; the H->L difference averages 28.9 slots against 12.4 slots that L actually accumulated since its own 500k ancestor, so the type-matched null applies about 2.3x the real post-midpoint change to H and cannot represent the reversal of H's private changes. The study measures 'typical 1M member vs typical 500k member, beyond a degraded H', not 'continued adaptation along a lineage'. Pairing each L with its own 500k ancestor (fully computable from existing checkpoints) makes the null the exact analogue of the divergence control and is my main recommendation; if declined, the protocol must say what is actually measured. (2) The confirmatory 7/8 L-N rule can be met with L about 0 (purifying only), and cannot be met reliably for moderate real effects: with unit-contrast SD about 0.15-0.4, P(met) is about 0.3-0.8 at a true contrast of 0.3 and about 0.1-0.4 at 0.2, so 'not met' is weak evidence and the M4 row that reads it as 'adaptation stalls, supporting the pivot' is not supported. The M4 table also lacks a purifying-only row, a founder-selection rule and a cluster-16 failure rule. (3) The swept-allele tail matters for one cluster-139 seed (6410007: H=33, L=47) and the opposite problem, L reverting to mu=33, appears in two cluster-139 seeds; cluster-33 is a clean post-sweep case (14/16 H draws already carry it), so the decision effectively rests on a single founder's test. (4) Power and independence: two pairs per unit, two units with H0==H1, four shared assay seeds, and single competitions that are position-by-seed noisy for near-clones (positions cancel exactly only for phenotypically identical genomes). The 500k midpoint is defensible (cluster-33 sweep done by 200-300k; 14/16 cluster-139 H draws swept) but 12 slots of true change may be too small to move a pairwise score by 0.1, so the study most likely tests only for large continued gains. Outcomes most at risk of misreading: 'not met' as stall; 'continued' in cluster-139 or cluster-4 where differences come from reversals or one large seed; a positive cluster-16 reading with no stated meaning.
review.limitations: No GPU work, competitions or protocol-stage writes were run. Read-only, with scratch hard links under runs/ created and removed by the tests and by one regeneration of the roster (output in my scratch folder). I did not re-verify the 54 frozen sources, the physical correctness of the 500k states beyond the frozen loader's receipt/hash/biology checks, or the competition executor on a non-founder ancestor. Lineage relationships come from the recorded mutation-parent edges and 100k-granular checkpoints; an ancestor lineage with a later child must be alive at 500k, and every A(L) was found there. Power figures are rough: unit-contrast SD is taken from the divergence control's per-draw dispersion (different comparison) and not from any continuation data. Disclosure: a mistyped loop of mine briefly wrote one scratch file named 'undefined' (synthetic analysis outputs, ~200 KB) into the repository root at 14:55; I deleted it and confirmed that no other file in the repository changed because of this review. Files being edited by the other engineer (endpoints.ts, analyze.ts, nullcal.ts, experiments/test) were ignored.

roundOneFindings.evidence: Each L is now paired with its own 500k ancestor. My own code path (ancestry-r2.ts: reads receipts, edge deltas and checkpoints directly, shares only @bl/schema decode) re-derived all 64 pairs: L lineage, ancestor lineage, ancestor genome, generations, lineage masses and H-to-L slot change all equal roster.json (0 mismatches). No lineage between L and A was born at or before 500k, so the H-to-L change is exactly the post-500k change along L's own lineage. The slot change never exceeds the generations walked (difference -3..0), which would not hold for a wrong parent path. The null is now the exact analogue of the divergence control's ancestor-descendant null.

Protocol 'What the outcomes mean for M4' now reads 'not met' as inconclusive with no stall claim, has a row for met-not-clearly-progressing (the purifying-only case), names cluster-33 as the deciding founder, gives a cluster-16 failure rule, and states power. I recomputed the power numbers (see N3): the statement is approximately right for SD about 0.25-0.3 and slightly optimistic at SD 0.4; wording nit only.

lateCertified (unit late lower bound > 0.10) is computed per unit and counted per founder; readContinuation requires >= 7 of 8 for the 'continued' and 'partly' readings. My exact-rational Python re-implementation matches the TypeScript analyzer on 7 synthetic scenarios (random, noisy, one flat scenario per reading branch, missing, both-extinct, lumpy 6/7/8 late seeds, near-threshold): counts, readings, unit/founder/pooled bounds and bootstrap all agree to 1e-12.

Not adopted, and the reason holds: the finding concerned a randomly drawn H being one member of a mutant swarm, which no longer applies when H is the ancestor of L on the same lineage. Residual interpretive limit (head-to-head non-transitivity) is not controllable cheaply and is not claimed against.

The protocol's pre-run facts now describe the new pairing, and every number checks out against roster.json, describeRoster() output and my own state decoding: cluster-33 H carries b2[PHOTO] > 62 in 14/16 pairs, neither H nor L in seed 6410002, no gain or loss, one L raised further (99 to 119, seed 6410006); cluster-139 H carries mu in 11/16, L in 13/16, both pairs of seed 6410007 gained (33 to 47), neither carries it in seed 6410002 (both) and seed 6410008 (one pair); medians 10/7/17/14 slots (ranges 7-15, 4-16, 5-27, 8-26); founder-lineage mass means 0.734M to 0.828M, 1.007M to 1.066M, 2.031M to 2.040M, 1.999M to 2.057M.

findings.detail: The independence caveat says a unit's two pairs 'can share an H'. They do in 10 of 32 units: cluster-33 5/8 (seeds 6410001, 02, 04, 06, 08), cluster-4 3/8 (01, 03, 07), cluster-139 2/8 (02, 07), cluster-16 0/8. For the deciding founder, 5 of 8 units therefore rest on one 500k ancestor lineage with two late descendants and four nulls of that same ancestor. Estimation is not biased (contrast is paired through H), but information per unit is lower and the 9/256 tail is more optimistic than the generic caveat suggests.

findings.detail: Power statement. (a) The SD 0.15-0.4 is derived from founder-versus-descendant spread in the divergence control, where genome distance is larger. L-versus-H and N-versus-H are near-clone comparisons (4-27 differing slots); the divergence findings note that competing identical genomes gives |score| averaging 0.69 per competition and that position cancellation is exact only for phenotypically identical genomes, so the spread here is unmeasured and may differ in either direction. (b) With 'certified' meaning observed mean > 0.10, P(7 of 8 seeds) for a true unit contrast d and unit SD s: s=0.15: 0.36 (d=0.2), 0.84 (0.3), 0.99 (0.4); s=0.25: 0.18, 0.47, 0.77, 0.93 (d=0.5); s=0.40: 0.11, 0.24, 0.43, 0.63 (d=0.5), 0.80 (0.6). 80% power needs d of about 0.29, 0.41, 0.60 for s of 0.15, 0.25, 0.40. 'About 0.4-0.5 or more reliably' is right for s up to about 0.3 and optimistic at 0.4. (c) The protocol's 'lower bound' wording can read as a confidence bound; it only widens for unavailable scores. There is no sampling uncertainty over the four assay seeds, so 'certified' means observed mean above 0.10 (the divergence findings state this caution; the continuation protocol does not).
findings.fix: Optional wording: 'the spread for near-clone pairs is unmeasured; with SD 0.15 / 0.25 / 0.4, 80% power needs a unit contrast of about 0.3 / 0.4 / 0.6', and 'bounds cover unavailable scores only; certified means the observed mean exceeds 0.10'. Does not change any decision rule, since the M4 table already treats every non-pass as inconclusive.

findings.detail: No competition with a non-founder ancestor has run on the GPU; the 8 opening replays and all audits use founder ancestors. I read executeAssay and discoveryCompetitionWorld: neither gates on founders, the world builder is genome-agnostic, every null genome is inside the slot bounds (checked), and the run test builds every one of the 1,536 requested worlds. A failure would surface in the first invocation (<= 600 s charge, supervision stops, no result affected). I did no GPU work.

findings.detail: Operational. The ledger charges wall-clock time, so a sleeping host is charged and the supervisor's watchdog (reservation + 120 s) would terminate a child that overran because of sleep, stopping supervision. Concurrent GPU work during the 5.4 h run would also slow competitions toward the 30,000 s cap (1.53x slack).
findings.fix: Run under caffeinate (or equivalent) and keep the GPU otherwise idle; no code change.

findings.detail: 'If cluster-16 reads continued or partly divergence, the assay or design is detecting something other than adaptation, since cluster-16 never improved over its founder.' Competition scores exist only at 100k and 1M, so a mid-run dip in cluster-16's competitive ability followed by recovery cannot be excluded; a positive cluster-16 reading would then be recovery, not an artefact. The rule is still a sensible guard.

independentChecks.name: definition: no overshoot, nearest born <= 500k equals nearest present

review.designAssessment: The rework fixes the one design flaw round 1 found. Each late genome is now compared with its own lineage's 500k ancestor, so the head-to-head is a within-lineage before/after, the change separating the pair is exactly the post-500k change, and the type-matched null is the same construct as the divergence control's. I re-derived all 64 pairs independently and could not break the definition: the nearest path lineage born at or before 500k is always the nearest one alive at 500k, the edge map is complete and unique, and the identity of L is bound to the loader-verified 1M sample. The reading logic, the per-seed late-certified count and the M4 table are consistent with each other and with the code, and the table is honest about what the study cannot show: no outcome supports a stall or the physics-change pivot, and only a clear positive reading for cluster-33 changes the picture. What the study measures is lineage-conditional progress: H is a small clade (median 0.4% of 500k mass) chosen because it gave rise to a 1M survivor, so L-versus-H is progress along realized successful lineages, not a population-average difference, which is what the question asks. The honest expectation is that the most likely result for the deciding founder is inconclusive: 14 of 16 cluster-33 ancestors already carry the sweep and the remaining post-500k change is 7-15 slots, so only a large late gain (unit contrast of roughly 0.4-0.6, depending on the unmeasured near-clone spread) passes the 7-of-8 rule. That is acceptable because the cost is compute on owned hardware at $0 and 5.4 hours, the table says so, and a pass would be informative. The remaining items (N1-N8) are wording, hardening and operational notes; none changes a decision rule or can cause a wrong or unrecoverable run. I would run it.
review.limitations: No GPU work and none of the run, supervise, candidate, stop or resolve stages were executed; the candidate CLI's full 32-history path was therefore not run end to end, although the ancestry() call it relies on is the one plan() ran in full and it reproduced the roster byte for byte. I did not re-verify the 54 frozen sources beyond what the divergence verify command and the continuation tests check, nor the physical correctness of the checkpoints beyond the frozen loader (I used its output through the generator and my own reads of the same files with receipt hash checks, but did not re-simulate). The no-resurrection argument for lineages rests on how the simulator mints lineage ids; I confirmed it empirically on every edge of all 32 normal histories rather than from the simulator source. Power figures use a normal approximation of the unit contrast with the protocol's SD range and are indicative only; the real spread of near-clone comparisons is unknown until data exist. The competition world was read, not run, for a non-founder ancestor. Disclosure: my work created and removed temporary directories runs/continuation-scratch-* (my plan regeneration, one negative test of historyAncestry, and the test suites); none remains. No repository file was modified by me; files modified during the review (tools/analyze.ts, experiments/endpoints.ts, experiments/preregistration.md, docs/plan.md, runs/nullcal/*) belong to the other engineer's amendment and were ignored.
